Study in the UK

One-year master’s degrees, two main intakes, and our own office in the country.

Enquire about the UK Find courses in the UK

At a glance

Main intakes
September, January
Master’s degree
1 year
Bachelor’s degree
3 years (4 in Scotland)
English tests
IELTS or PTE; some universities accept TOEFL, Duolingo or Class 12 English marks
Visa
Student visa

Why students choose the UK

  • Most master’s degrees take one year, so you pay living costs for one year instead of two.
  • Two main intakes, September and January, give you a second chance if you miss the first.
  • Some universities accept strong Class 12 English marks in place of a language test.
  • Eesha has its own office in the UK, so you have a contact in the country.

Popular subjects

  • Business and management
  • Computer science and data
  • Engineering
  • Public health and nursing
  • Law

Documents you will need

  • Passport
  • Class 10, Class 12 and degree mark sheets and certificates
  • English test score, or a waiver from the university
  • Statement of purpose and letters of recommendation
  • CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) from your university
  • Bank statements or an education loan sanction letter
  • Tuberculosis test certificate from an approved clinic

After you graduate

After your degree you can apply for the Graduate Route visa, which lets you stay in the UK and work or look for work.

Visa and work rules change. Your counsellor will confirm what applies on the date you apply.

Universities in the UK

See their courses

  • University of Birmingham

    Birmingham

    A Russell Group research university in the UK’s second-largest city.

  • University of Leeds

    Leeds

    A Russell Group university whose business school holds triple accreditation.

  • University of Glasgow

    Glasgow

    Founded in 1451. A Russell Group university and one of the oldest in the English-speaking world.

  • University of Leicester

    Leicester

    A research university known for space science. DNA fingerprinting was invented here.

  • Coventry University

    Coventry

    Known for automotive and engineering courses, with several intakes a year on many master’s degrees.

  • University of Hertfordshire

    Hatfield

    A short train ride from central London, and popular for computing and business courses.

  • University of Greenwich

    London

    Its main campus is the Old Royal Naval College, a World Heritage Site on the Thames.

  • Northumbria University

    Newcastle upon Tyne

    Based in Newcastle with a second campus in London. Its business school is AACSB accredited.

  • Sheffield Hallam University

    Sheffield

    One of the UK’s largest universities, with work placements built into many courses.

  • Anglia Ruskin University

    Cambridge and Chelmsford

    Campuses in Cambridge and Chelmsford, with September and January intakes.

  • Teesside University

    Middlesbrough

    Known for computing, animation and games courses.
